pageCache.pageTitle: Wraparound Care - Beacon Hill Primary School
pageCache.text:
Wraparound Care
We provide a welcoming, happy, safe, warm and stimulating environment for all children who attend the the breakfast and after school care club. The club runs every day during term time and is open to all children who attend the school. Please see the information detailed below which includes a registration form which must be completed before your child attends the club. Parents are able to pay for the club through the Arbor on-line payments system and we can also take childcare vouchers for the club.
Do pop into the school office if you require any further information about wraparound care.
Online Booking
All bookings should be made via Arbor. Bookings must be made by Friday morning prior to the following week when the care is required as appropriate staffing support and food provisions must be planned in advance. Bookings should not be made via email or phone unless Arbor is not working. Please do not book on the day. We understand however, that there may be certain emergency situations, and we will endeavour to help on those occasions.
Cancellations
If your child is unwell, they will be marked as absent on the Breakfast and After School Care Club register and you will not be charged. Cancellations on the day for reasons other than absence will be charged at the normal rate.
Session Timings
Breakfast club runs from 7.45 to the beginning of the school day – Browns children will be taken to their classrooms by a member of staff.
The first after school session runs from the end of the school day until 4.20pm (Monday-Friday). All children who are booked in for this session only MUST be collected by this time. If your child attends for only part of the session, the full fee will still need to be charged. If your child is collected after 4.20pm you will be charged for the second session as well.
The second session runs from 4.21pm to 6pm (Monday - Thursday only) and all children in this session MUST be collected by 6pm when the school closes for the evening. There will be a late payment charge of £15.00 applied if you child is not picked up by 6.00 pm. Please see the document below for charging information. The school operates the wraparound care club as a business and has to meet its costs in order to run.
Payment
Payment should be made either online via Arbor or with childcare vouchers. Please ensure that payments are made in a timely fashion to avoid large bills mounting up.
Collection of Children
If you are unable to collect your child yourself, the expectation is that arrangements will be made so please ensure that the office have been informed as to who will be coming to collect.

pageCache.pageTitle: School Clubs - Beacon Hill Primary School
pageCache.text:
School Clubs
We offer a range of clubs for children to enjoy, both after school and during lunchtime. These include activities such as Spanish, Minibeasts, Craft Club and a variety of sports clubs, giving pupils the opportunity to explore new interests and develop their skills in a fun and supportive environment.
Information about clubs is shared with parents via the Arbor system at the start of each term. Paper copies are also provided for children whose parents are not yet registered.
We kindly ask parents to inform the school if their child is unable to attend a session for any reason. Collection time for most clubs is 4:20 pm, with Minibeasts finishing slightly later at 4:30 pm.

pageCache.pageTitle: PE and Sport Premium Funding - Beacon Hill Primary School
pageCache.text:
PE and Sport Premium Funding
At Beacon Hill Primary, we are passionate about instilling a love for physical activity and healthy living in all our students. We achieve this through a combination of:
High-Quality Curriculum: Our PE program features a diverse range of activities, from team sports like netball, basketball, and cricket to tag rugby, rounders, and dance.
Weekly Sessions: Every week, your child will have dedicated PE sessions ensuring consistent development and a chance to practice their skills regularly. There are also an array of after school clubs to continue to keep active.
Through this well-rounded program, our goal is to equip each student with the knowledge, motivation, and practical skills they need to lead a healthy and active life, both during their time at Crondall and beyond.
PE and Sport Premium Funding
The funding has been provided by the Government to achieve self-sustaining improvement in the quality of PE and sport in primary schools. All schools with 17 or more primary-aged pupils receive a lump sum of money plus a premium of £10 per pupil.
At Beacon Hill Primary School the Sports Premium allocation is used to promote enjoyment and engagement in sport and exercise and healthy lifestyles by:
Providing additional training in PE skills of teaching staff in the school; to develop the opportunities for extra-curricular clubs and to organise more intra-school competitions for the school Houses.
Providing additional resources for PE and school sport for pupils now and in the future.
The profile of PE and sport is raised across the school.
Improving the outdoor learning environment for extending our outdoor PE provision.
By 31 July each year, schools that receive PE and sport premium funding must publish,

SEND
Our SENCO (Special Educational Needs Co-ordinator) is Mrs Jess Randall.
Any parent who is concerned about how the special needs of their child will be met should contact the school’s SENCO via the school office or email senco@beacon-hill.surrey.sch.uk, 01428 605597. Our SEND Governor is Angela Rayne and she can be contacted via the school office.
All the teachers at Beacon Hill Primary School are teachers of children with special educational needs. As such Beacon Hill School adopts a ‘whole school approach’ which involves all the staff adhering to a model of good practice. All teaching staff are committed to identifying and providing for the needs of all children, irrespective of need in an inclusive environment.
The special needs of the majority of our children are provided for within the framework of the normal curriculum with the emphasis on the quality of learning and the desire for all pupils to make significant progress. The impact of any interventions that are in place for individual children is evidence-based and assessed on a regular basis to give next steps for the child, teachers and support staff.
The School’s policy on Special Educational Needs complies fully with recent Government legislation and with the revised Code of Practice; it is monitored and reviewed regularly by both staff and governors. Both the school’s SEND Policy and Accessibility Plan (Physical Environment) Policy can be found in the Policies section of this website.
To explore Surrey's Local Offer please visit the following site: https://www.surreylocaloffer.org.uk/
This is an extensive website which details all of the services and provision on offer within Surrey.
The documents below answer FAQs about SEND provision at Beacon Hill Primary School and detail what SEN provision we we currently offer children.

Attendance
Regular and punctual school attendance is essential if pupils are to take full advantage of the educational opportunities available to them.
Attendance
Regular attendance is vital if your child is to truly succeed and reach their true potential. We kindly request your support and encouragement to ensure your child attends school regularly and arrives on time. Regular attendance not only positively impacts your child's academic progress but also fosters a sense of responsibility and commitment. A child’s success at school is likely to be affected negatively if their attendance is poor. Those who do not attend regularly may fall behind in their learning, leading to underachievement, both academically and socially.
To aid you in promoting good attendance, we want to assure you that Beacon Hill Primary School provides you with professional, quality information and advice. We will communicate with you through various channels such as telephone conversations, parents’ evenings, school reports, and our school attendance webpage. This will ensure that you stay informed about school attendance and have access to any resources or support that may be required.
Punctuality
The school day starts at 8.45am when all pupils should be in their classroom, in preparation for the register being taken.
Being in school on time every day, ready to learn, is vital. Arriving on time allows your child to settle well and have the best start to their day. If your child arrives after 9.00am your child is late and has missed the start of the school day. Even being only a few minutes late can unsettle your child which is not the best start for their day and should be avoided wherever possible.
Attendance and punctuality are tracked throughout the year, and you will be informed of your child’s attendance and punctuality throughout the year at parents’ evenings.
How to report an absence
If your child cannot come to school because of illness, you should advise the school on the first day of absence by contacting the school, stating your child’s name, their class and the reason for their absence,
01428 605597 or if you are unable to get through, please use the answer phone facility.
info@beacon-hill.surrey.sch.uk
If no message is received, we will contact you to find out the reason for absence, this is called First Day Response.
We ask families to make any medical appointments out of school hours wherever possible. However, if this is not possible, we can authorise absences for appointments on completion of a Medical Appointment Leave of Absence Request Form which can be downloaded here or collected from the school office.
We do not authorise holidays in term time. All holiday absences must be made by completing a Withdrawal from Learning Form which can be downloaded here or collected from the school office.
If unauthorised holidays are taken during term time a financial penalty may be imposed.

pageCache.pageTitle: Moving on to Secondary School - Beacon Hill Primary School
pageCache.text:
Moving on to Secondary School
Local secondary schools typically hold Open Evenings during the Autumn term, providing Parents/Carers with the opportunity to visit and learn more about the schools before making their decision.
Induction days are scheduled by secondary schools in the Summer term, and Parents/Carers will be notified of the specific dates as they may vary.
In preparation for the transition to secondary school, during the summer term, Year 6 teachers deliver PSHE sessions. Additionally, staff from the secondary schools visit to meet the children, and an assembly is held to allow students to ask questions. Year 6 teachers also ensure a thorough handover with key staff members from the secondary schools, while SEND teams from the respective schools coordinate with our Inclusion team for a smooth transition process.
Should additional support be needed, extra visits and transition sessions can be arranged. The Home-School Link Worker (HSLW), in collaboration with the Resilience & Wellbeing Support Assistant (RWSA), organise these additional sessions. The HSLW also maintains close communication with the secondary schools to ensure a seamless transition for all students.
